methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: While considering the energy consumption of a defined amount of product is useful for the comparison of the performance of two plants and management decisions, it does not provide reliable information to verify specified machine-based consumption data or for a source-related cost allocation as a basis for a weak point analysis

paper_type.evidence_quote: To obtain representative data, five bottling plants using typical packaging types (returnable glass and PET bottles) and products (water, soft drinks, and beer) were considered for the data analysis.

level_3b.evidence_quote: bottling and packaging machines in the food and beverage industry

stage1.notes: Empirical energy-measurement study across 5 bottling plants / 20 machines; critiques specific-energy KPIs (kWh/1000 fillings) and proposes an operational-state-based energy-consumption model -> eligible. Multi-plant empirical -> multi-case (not methodological/theoretical, which excludes empirical). Sector = food & beverage bottling/packaging (discrete), not on closed continuous-process list.

type_of_organisation.evidence_quote: packaging and bottling machines differ from other manufacturing plants

evidence_quote: the energy consumption for a specific number of products (e.g., kWh/1000 fillings)
the energy consumption of food-packaging and bottling machines is described by a limited discrete number of energy states related to the operational state
